gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Anker SOLIX S2000, its #2 pick for a 12 V fridge, has no 12 V car output at all. Anker's spec table lists only USB-C (100 W + 15 W), USB-A (12 W) and AC outputs. On the S2000 a 12 V fridge has to run from the fridge's AC adapter with the inverter on, and Anker rates that state at 6 W 'Active Idle Power'. Over 72 h that is about 432 Wh of overhead before the fridge draws anything.
standout_why: Compared against: the solarwaypoint.com C2000 Gen 2 vs AC200L vs DELTA 2 Max page, which lists '12V accessory sockets' with no V/A rating, no idle figures and nothing on the S2000; the cited EcoFlow DELTA 2 Max manuals, which cover only EcoFlow; and the result titles, none of which is about the S2000 (they cover DELTA 2 Max, AC200L, F2000 and C2000 Gen 2). I could not read buyerdecision.com/tools/power-station-reality-check (HTTP 403) or the two stationarena.com pages (TLS certificate error), so a car-port table there can't be ruled out. Even so, none of those result titles names the S2000. ChatGPT's own answer called the S2000 'best for portability' for a 12 V fridge and told the shopper to plug the fridge into the 12 V car socket.
decides: The S2000 should come off a 12 V-fridge list, or be shown as AC-only with an idle penalty. Of the ~2 kWh units, the ones that hold the pick are those with a real 12 V car port: Anker's C2000 Gen 2 (12 V / 10 A), EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max and BLUETTI Elite 200 V2. A normalised idle column also matters for 3 days. Makers state idle three different ways: Anker S2000 gives 'Active Idle 6 W / System Standby 2 W', Anker C2000 Gen 2 gives '9 W idle' with no conditions, and Jackery gives no figure, but The Solar Lab measured about 17 W with the inverter on. Over 72 h those figures range from about 144 Wh to about 1,224 Wh. That is the footnote: run the fridge from the 12 V port with the inverter off, never from AC.
